messages:
sam: heads up — running into import issues using the JS SDK in a Vercel Edge function. It works locally with node, but Edge build fails with 'default export not found' errors.
alyssa: can you paste the snippet + package.json? Edge + ESM quirks usually.
sam: sure — minimal example:
```js
// edge-function.js
const redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.generate('hello');
```
package.json:
```json
{ "name": "edge-app", "type": "module", "dependencies": { "@redwood/inference": "^1.2.0" } }
```
Error: "TypeError: redwood.default is not a constructor" when deployed. Works with `node edge-function.js` (local dev).
michael: yep this is the classic CJS/ESM interop mismatch. a few approaches depending on the runtime and how the SDK exports things. quick notes: 1) Edge runtimes like Vercel/Cloudflare run as ESM; 2) if the SDK ships both CJS and ESM entrypoints, bundlers sometimes pick the wrong one; 3) TypeScript compiler flags can affect default import behavior.
alyssa: TL;DR fixes: (A) Use ESM import syntax in Edge: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` or `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` depending on our export. (B) If using require, use `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference').default || require('@redwood/inference')`. (C) Set "type":"module" or adjust bundler.
sam: thanks — tried `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` in the edge file and now it runs, but TypeScript complains: "Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/inference'". Our types are missing in the package?
michael: two things to check: 1) ensure SDK published includes .d.ts and package.json has "types" field. 2) if the package exports types only under `dist/index.d.ts` we need the package.json `types` pointing there. For quick local fix, add `declare module '@redwood/inference'` to a `global.d.ts`. But we should fix upstream.
alyssa: for the docs side — our README currently shows `const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference')` in the quickstart. That is probably the source of confusion. We should: 1) show both ESM and CJS examples, 2) clearly document default vs named exports, and 3) add an Edge quickstart snippet.
sam: can we also mention TS compiler options? I had to set `esModuleInterop: true` to get `import Redwood from '...'` to type-check in a TS project that transpiles to CommonJS for older servers.
michael: yes add a short table:
- ESM runtime (Edge, modern Node): `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` or `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` if named-only.
- CommonJS runtime: `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference').default || require('@redwood/inference')`
- TypeScript: recommend `esModuleInterop: true, allowSyntheticDefaultImports: true` in tsconfig when consumers want `import default` syntax.
alyssa: actionable items: @michael can you open a PR to update README + quickstart to include both examples and an Edge snippet? Also @michael please confirm package.json has "exports" map that points to ESM and CJS correctly and that `types` is present.
michael: will do. opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/789 — it adds: - ESM + CJS examples - Edge runtime section - note about TS flags - fallback require pattern. also added docs-bot comment to create an arcade example in examples/edge.
docs-bot: created issue #312 in docs: "Clarify JS SDK import patterns (ESM/CJS/Edge/TS)" and added to docs backlog.
sam: awesome thanks! once PR lands i'll re-test and report back. one more ask — can we add a short section in Deploy > Edge about common bundler pitfalls (esbuild, webpack) and `package.json` "type" field? i got bitten by `type: module` earlier.
alyssa: yes add that to docs PR. also consider adding a tiny automated test in CI that runs the example in a node --experimental-fetch / edge-like build to catch regressions.
michael: noted. I'll include a small CI job that runs the edge example with `@vercel/ncc` or esbuild to ensure exports are correct.
sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
